description:
**Summary:**

Provides analysis and interpretation of the customers’ and/or merchants’ financial status for proper evaluation of risk and the establishment of proper credit limits. Interacts with sales support, customer service, and accounts receivable in reconciling accounts. Prepares recommendations and makes credit approval decisions on new accounts. Analyzes and reports on credit memo and write-off activity. Monitors and communicates credit concerns to management. This job is not for those responsible for placing routine calls to customers for collection of past due accounts. This role is focused on policy decisions/judgment regarding credit offers.

**Duties & Responsibilities:**

  

**Job title:** EMEA Credit Control Analyst

**Department:** Finance and Administration

**Immediate Manager:** EMEA Sales Controller/ EMEA Controller

**Location:** Pune, India

**About VIAVI Solutions**

VIAVI (NASDAQ: VIAV) has a 90+ year history of technical innovations that have evolved to keep pace and address our customers’ most pressing business issues. We make equipment, software, and systems that help to plan, deploy, certify, monitor, and optimize all kinds of networks - like those for mobile phones, service providers, large businesses, and data centers. We are also at the forefront of optical security – we bend light to develop and deliver optical solutions that provide security to the world’s currencies and safety and performance applications for consumer electronics and spectrometry.

We are the people behind the products that help keep the world connected – at home, school, work, at play, and everywhere in between. VIAVI employees are fierce about supporting customer success and we welcome people who bring their best every day to the company - to question, to collaborate and to push for solutions that will delight our customers.

**Job Description**

The Credit Control Analyst is responsible for assessing customer credit risk, maintaining appropriate credit limits and payment terms, managing credit holds, and supporting the timely collection of outstanding receivables.

The role works closely with customers, Sales, Order Management, Accounts Receivable (GSSC), Business Unit Finance, and other internal stakeholders to manage credit exposure, resolve account issues, support order release decisions, and minimize the risk of bad debt.

The position requires strong financial analysis, communication, reconciliation, and organizational skills, together with the ability to balance commercial requirements against the organization’s credit risk policies.

**Key Responsibilities**

**1. Credit Hold and Order Release Management**

* Monitor credit hold reports, blocked orders, shipment holds, and the central credit inbox on a daily basis.
* Assess credit availability for booked and scheduled orders before approving order or shipment release.
* Review order backlog, bookings, shipment activity, outstanding balances, and sales pipeline information to identify potential credit exposure.
* Apply or release credit holds at customer, account, order, shipment, or order-line level in accordance with the company’s credit policy and approval framework.

**2. Reporting and Performance Monitoring**

* Prepare regular reporting on blocked orders, CN, disputed balances, and customer credit exposure.
* Monitor and report on operational credit control activities, including: Credit releases completed, Blocked orders reviewed and released, Credit note approvals supported, Proforma invoices issued have been paid, Credit limit changes processed, Customer profiles updated, Payment-term exceptions reviewed
* Maintain accurate reporting data and provide commentary on significant movements, emerging risks, and overdue accounts.
* Assist management with ad hoc credit reporting.
* Support quarter-end and year-end financial close activities relevant to credit control and accounts receivable.

**3. Compliance and Internal Controls**

* Ensure that credit assessments, limit changes, payment terms, and credit hold decisions are appropriately documented and approved.
* Maintain evidence supporting new-customer payment terms and approved deviations for existing customers.
* Maintain complete and audit-ready records of credit decisions, approvals, and customer correspondence.
* Support internal, external, and control-related audit requests.
* Follow company policies relating to credit management, financial controls, data protection, and customer information.

**4. Process Improvement**

* Participate in credit control process-improvement initiatives.
* Perform ad-hoc root-cause analysis on recurring billing, customer-data, and order-release issues if required.
* Support the standardization and documentation of credit control processes.
* Assist with testing or implementing system and process changes affecting credit and collections.

**5. Credit Assessment and Risk Management**

* Assist credit assessments for new and existing customers with relevant credit reports and other relevant credit information.
* Review requests for extended or non-standard payment terms and ensure that the appropriate approvals and supporting documentation are obtained.

**Job Skills & Requirements:**

* Degree or professional qualification in Finance, Accounting, Business, or a related discipline
* Experience working within an international or multinational organization.
* Understanding of the Quote-to-Cash or Order-to-Cash process
* Exposure to SOX/Internal controls and supporting audits, with strong documentation and compliance focus
* Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills
* Proven ability in working under pressure and meeting deadlines

description:
**Company Description**

IntegriChain is the data and application backbone for market access departments of Life Sciences manufacturers. We deliver the data, the applications, and the business process infrastructure for patient access and therapy commercialization. More than 250 manufacturers rely on our ICyte Platform to orchestrate their commercial and government payer contracting, patient services, and distribution channels. ICyte is the first and only platform that unites the financial, operational, and commercial data sets required to support therapy access in the era of specialty and precision medicine. With ICyte, Life Sciences innovators can digitalize their market access operations, freeing up resources to focus on more data-driven decision support. With ICyte, Life Sciences innovators are digitalizing labor-intensive processes – freeing up their best talent to identify and resolve coverage and availability hurdles and to manage pricing and forecasting complexity.

We are headquartered in Philadelphia, PA (USA), with offices in: Ambler, PA (USA); Pune, India; and Medellín, Colombia. For more information, visit www.integrichain.com, or follow us on Twitter @IntegriChain and LinkedIn.

 **Job Description**

As a Government Pricing (GP) Analyst, you will help pharmaceutical and biotech manufacturers meet their price reporting obligations under U.S. Government Programs. This work directly supports how patients access therapies through Medicaid, Medicare, the VA, and the 340B program, and it is held to a high standard of accuracy and compliance.

You will join IntegriChain’s Net Revenue and Compliance team in Pune, which provides managed services and business process outsourcing to biopharmaceutical clients. You will work closely with GP managers, technical teams, and U.S.-based client stakeholders.

This role suits someone early in their finance or accounting career who enjoys working with data, takes pride in getting the numbers right, and wants to build expertise in a high-demand area of the pharma industry. Prior Government Pricing experience is helpful but not required; we will train you.

**Working hours:** This is a hybrid role based in Pune. Because you will work closely with U.S.-based clients and managers, the role requires some overlap with U.S. Eastern working hours

**What you’ll do to thrive in this role:**

* **Government Price calculations;**
* Prepare, validate, calculate, and analyse price reporting required under the following U.S. government programs: the Medicaid Drug Rebate Program, Medicare Part B, the VA Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), and the 340B Drug Pricing Program.
* Prepare and validate the underlying data for price types including Average Manufacturer Price (AMP), Best Price (BP), Average Sales Price (ASP), Non-Federal Average Manufacturer Price (Non-FAMP), Federal Ceiling Price (FCP), Industrial Funding Fee (IFF), and Unit Rebate Amount (URA).
* Deliver accurate, on-time calculations for assigned products on a monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting schedule.
* Review calculations with the client reviewer and obtain sign-off, following all required SOPs, before prices are submitted to government agencies (such as CMS, VA, and DoD) or shared with internal Medicaid rebate users.

**Data management and analysis;**

Review and maintain the master data used across all government pricing calculations.

* Manage each client’s class-of-trade hierarchy and clients PHS eligibility and ensure every incoming transaction is correctly tagged and mapped. Perform accurate COT and PHS validations.
* Analyze calculation results, investigate variances, and identify their root cause.
* Partner with clients, the client reviewer, and the technical team to resolve system, data, and process issues.

**Controls and documentation;**

* Document all revisions and adjustments made to client data in line with financial controls and standard operating procedures.
* Maintain SOPs, SOX documentation, and evidence of work supporting each price calculation.

**Where You’ll Grow:**

* As you build confidence in the core role, you will also gain exposure to adjacent areas of Net Revenue and Compliance.
* **Gross-to-Net (GTN)**: accrual close, forecasting, and related deliverables. transactional data, general ledger reconciliations, and data extraction from internal, external, and client systems
* **State Price Transparency Reporting (SPTR)**: reporting requirements and the U.S. state regulations behind them. portfolio set up activities and preparation of client reports.

  
**Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s degree in commerce, Finance, Accounting, or Business.
* 2–4 years of experience in financial analysis, accounting, or a data-intensive operations role, ideally in the pharmaceutical, healthcare, or life sciences industry.
* Strong Excel skills (e.g., pivot tables, lookups, and working with large datasets), plus working knowledge of Word and PowerPoint.
* Sharp attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy in financial data.
* Ability to manage multiple deliverables at once and meet fixed deadlines.
* Clear written and spoken English, with the confidence to communicate with managers and U.S.-based clients.
* A proactive, self-directed working style, including knowing when to escalate an issue.

**Nice to have**

* Exposure to U.S. government pricing, rebates, chargebacks, or contract pricing.
* Experience with Model N, Revitas, iContracts, or SAP.
* Familiarity with SOX controls or experience working in an audited environment.
* Experience with SQL or Microsoft Access.
* A postgraduate or professional qualification such as an MBA (Finance), M. Com, or CA/CMA (Intermediate or qualified)

  
**Additional Information**

**What does IntegriChain have to offer?**

* Mission driven: Work with the purpose of helping to improve patients' lives!
* Excellent and affordable medical benefits + non-medical perks including Student Loan Reimbursement, Flexible Paid Time Off and Paid Parental Leave
* 401(k) Plan with a Company Match to prepare for your future

The Hotel Accountant will be responsible for maintaining accurate day to day financial records, monitoring hotel revenue and expenses, completing reconciliations, supporting statutory compliance, and providing timely financial information to Management.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

* Daily Accounting Operations

Maintain the daily books of accounts and ensure all financial transactions are recorded correctly.

Record sales, purchases, expenses, receipts and payments on a timely basis.

Check cash collections and ensure that deposits and records are properly reconciled.

Maintain petty cash records along with all supporting documents.

* Hotel Revenue and PMS Reconciliation

Match daily room revenue with the hotel PMS records.

Verify occupancy, room rates, discounts, cancellations and complimentary room entries.

Reconcile OTA bookings, collections and commissions.

Monitor corporate credit bills and outstanding balances.

Investigate and report any difference between operational records and accounting records.

* Banking and Collection Control

Complete regular bank reconciliations.

Record cash, card, UPI, cheque and online collections accurately.

Monitor bank deposits and ensure all collections are properly accounted for.

Follow up on pending, unidentified or unreconciled transactions.

* Vendor Accounts and Payments

Check vendor invoices against purchase records and supporting documents.

Maintain accurate vendor ledgers.

Prepare payment schedules for Management approval.

Monitor outstanding vendor balances and agreed credit periods.

Ensure that vendor payments are processed only after the required verification and approval.

* GST, TDS and Statutory Requirements

Maintain accurate GST and TDS records.

Prepare the accounting information required for GST and TDS returns.

Check GST details on purchase invoices.

Coordinate with the CA and tax consultant for statutory filings.

Maintain all supporting records required for compliance and audits.

* Payroll and Employee Records

Assist Management and HR with preparation of monthly salary information.

Maintain records relating to employee advances, deductions and recoveries.

Coordinate with HR regarding payroll related accounting information.

Maintain records required for PF, ESI and other applicable statutory requirements.

* MIS and Management Information

Prepare regular financial and operational reports for Management, including the following.

Daily Revenue Report

Daily Collection Report

Bank and Cash Position

Outstanding Receivables

Vendor Payables

OTA Reconciliation

Corporate Outstanding Report

Monthly Profit and Loss Data

Expense Analysis

GST and TDS Summary

* Audit and Record Management

Keep bills, invoices, vouchers and other financial documents properly filed and accessible.

Assist internal, statutory and tax auditors with the information and documents they require.

Coordinate with auditors and consultants as directed by Management.

Ensure accounting records remain complete, accurate and up to date.

KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS

The Accountant will be evaluated on the accuracy and timeliness of accounting entries, completion of daily revenue reconciliation, accuracy of cash and bank reconciliation, correctness of OTA reconciliation, timely preparation of MIS, control over receivables and payables, support for timely GST and TDS compliance, proper maintenance of records, and minimisation of accounting discrepancies.

SKILLS AND QUALIFICATIONS

A B.Com, M.Com or equivalent accounting qualification is preferred.

The candidate should have 2 to 5 years of relevant accounting experience, with hotel or hospitality accounting experience preferred.
